title: Correlation Swaps, Quanto Options and Concentration Ratio

maps.tested: A sleeper: the importance sheet is lukewarm on the chapter, but seven recall sources name it, several as a numerical. That divergence is itself the signal: do not deprioritise this on the strength of the sheet.
maps.specifics: Reported as '1 on correlation swap return' (numerical), 'correlation swap' (twice, separate sittings), 'swap correlation', and 'quanto options'. The correlation-swap payoff is realised average pairwise correlation minus the fixed strike, times notional. The handwritten sheet also flags concentration ratio concept and calculation from the same chapter.

maps.tested: The handwritten sheet names it as a second must-do from the correlation chapter: 'concentration ratio concept and calculation as well.'
maps.specifics: LO 8.g links correlation risk to systemic and concentration risk. The 2007-09 narrative (LO 8.b) is the case-study layer. Low recall evidence, but the sheet is specific enough that the calculation is worth one pass.

vardeezReading: MR-8: Moderate, with the note "a) Quanto Option & Correlation Swap b) Concentration Ratio Concept & Calculation as well".

selectors.name: Correlation swap payoff, fixed-rate payer
selectors.what: Payoff to the fixed-rate payer (the correlation buyer) = N x (realised correlation - fixed correlation), where realised correlation is the simple average of the pairwise correlations (the i > j cells, 2/(n^2 - n) times their sum). Example: pairs 0.5, 0.3, 0.1 give 0.3; fixed 10%, notional USD 1,000,000, payer receives USD 200,000.
selectors.theory: What a correlation swap exchanges (a known fixed correlation for the realised, unknown one), why paying fixed is buying correlation, why only the off-diagonal pairs enter the average, and why the fixed payer gains when realised correlation exceeds the strike.

selectors.name: Correlation swap payoff, seller's side
selectors.what: The same swap from the fixed-rate receiver (the correlation seller): payoff = N x (fixed correlation - realised correlation), with volatilities and maturity given as irrelevant inputs.
selectors.theory: The seller's payoff is the mirror image of the buyer's; selling correlation gains when realised correlation falls below the strike, and the volatilities play no part in the payoff.

selectors.name: Correlation swap return, solve for strike
selectors.what: Return per unit notional = payoff / N = realised correlation - fixed correlation for the payer; given the return and the pairwise correlations, reverse-solve for the fixed strike.
selectors.theory: Per unit of notional the payoff is the gap between realised and fixed correlation, so the strike is the realised average less the return (for the payer).

selectors.name: Quanto option correlation risk and direction
selectors.what: A quanto lets a domestic investor swap a foreign-currency option payoff into home currency at a fixed exchange rate; the price depends on the correlation between the underlying and the exchange rate (domestic per foreign), and the more positive the correlation, the cheaper the quanto.

selectors.name: Concentration ratio and joint default
selectors.what: Concentration ratio = 1/n for n equal loans (ten equal loans: 0.1; one loan: 1); a lower ratio and a lower default correlation reduce the creditor's worst case. Joint default of two binomial events: P(X and Y) = rho x sqrt(PX(1 - PX) x PY(1 - PY)) + PX x PY, e.g. two loans with PD 10% give 10% at rho = 1, 5.5% at 0.5, 1% at 0.
selectors.theory: Why spreading exposure over more names lowers the ratio and diversifies default risk only when default correlation is below 1 (at rho = 1 the loans default together and the worst case is unchanged), and why intra-sector defaults are more highly correlated than inter-sector ones.
